decisions.decision: Phase 1 is an installed local Rust/OpenTUI TUI and embedded web app on one authenticated Rust/Tokio/SQLite daemon. Hosted account/control-plane, pairing/tunnel and native phone apps are later phases.
Native extensions/skills/commands/hooks are Phase 1. Arbitrary Solid/TS UI-plugin compatibility is not claimed; any optional JS host is a separate explicit later-phase compatibility project.

Proposed required desktop matrix: macOS arm64, Linux x86_64, Windows x86_64. A missing runner, native library, sandbox or required signing identity blocks that declared target; no silent platform downgrade.

Proposed canonical command follows current Cargo target oc2, preserving opencode-rk compatibility and deciding the legacy opencode2 alias explicitly. Never overwrite the user's existing opencode command.

Required local web search/deep-research and voice/dictation remain included by default. Missing real adapters/permissions/budget block those packages; removing them requires an explicit user-approved deferral and narrower release claim.
All destructive tests/imports use generated data or an explicitly approved copy. The existing user OpenCode database, provider edits and credential files are not fixtures.

Minimum safe subagent execution/leases/independent verification is required to build Phase 1. A standalone production twenty-worker controller, general workflow-builder and speculative autocodegen product are later scope, not hidden additions.

Keep canonical OpenCode baseline 95daf906 intact. Explicitly evaluate the previously observed 45ad8dc TUI pages/commands as the proposed Phase 1 presentation target; classify additions once and freeze, rather than chase live dev.

Only documented authorized provider auth flows are supported. Compatible endpoint/API-key setup is required; actual OAuth availability and consent must be verified before claiming support. No impersonation/evasion or automatic access to unrelated credential stores.

Safe export/import and a redacted revocable local share view are Phase 1. Public hosted sharing needs a separately approved deployment/auth scope; it is not fabricated as a localhost link that other people can reach.

The shared local client/API/event contract is required. Full external ACP/SDK/server spawner and remote workspace-proxy compatibility can be a named later-phase compatibility slice; existing regression tests are preserved.
